\begin{example} \end{example}[Cellular homology of closed orientable surfaces] ↗ thm:cellular-singular-homology-isomorphic ↗ ex:sphere-two-cells 1. ch2:2.36\group Cellular Homology

For the genus-$g$ orientable surface with one $0$-cell, $2g$ $1$-cells, and one $2$-cell attached by $\prod _i[a_i,b_i]$, both cellular boundary maps vanish. Thus $H_0=H_2=\mathbb {Z}$ and $H_1=\mathbb {Z}^{2g}$. \end{example}
